_comment: The first of the four famous places (2026-09-04, section 60I), and the one whose card decided its scene. It was written as a brownstone side street in autumn -- the rule being that a famous place is a street, not a sign, because BASE_NEGATIVES forbid lettering -- and the owner asked for Times Square itself, signs and all. He was right that the square is the picture people forward; the rule survives one layer down: the tape prompt still forbids readable words and brand logos, so on the tape the billboards are lit colour panels rather than adverts, and the negatives say so twice. The card (assets/places/new-york-times-square.jpg) shows the square at night with nobody in it, a police kiosk and a hot-dog cart on the island, and this preset describes exactly that.
label: Times Square, at night
_passersby_comment: Times Square with nobody in it is the one thing nobody has ever seen. Strangers stay away from the lens; the composer writes that clause, not this file.

prompt._comment: The billboards are the light source and the era at once: in 2003 they were painted panels and early video screens stacked up the wedge, not one wraparound LED skin, and a 2003 holiday tape of the square is nothing but them. The police kiosk on the island and the cart under its umbrella are what put a person somewhere specific in the square rather than in front of a backdrop.
prompt.scene: Times Square in New York at night, the wedge of buildings above the crossing stacked with lit billboards and glowing screens, yellow cabs waiting at the lights, a police kiosk on the traffic island, a hot-dog cart under a red and white umbrella, wet pavement and crosswalk stripes holding every light
prompt.light: the whole square lit from above by the billboards, cold white from the screens and warm red from the signs mixing on the wet ground, sodium street lamps under it all, the sky above gone to black
prompt.lens: wide from the pavement looking up the square, the far end going soft behind the glare, every screen drawing a hard block of light, a little barrel bend at the edges
prompt.framing: chest-up on the traffic island, the billboards stacked up behind and the cabs passing
prompt._moment: What is HAPPENING, not what is in frame. A brief with no action in it is a portrait brief, and the model answers it with a portrait -- squared to the camera, arms hanging, waiting. Somebody caught halfway through something ordinary is what a real snapshot looks like.
prompt.moment: turning on the spot to take it all in, one arm half raised towards the tallest screen
prompt.eraProps: a yellow cab with a roof light, a payphone bank on the corner, a newspaper vending box, a hot-dog cart under a striped umbrella, a disposable camera with a wind-on wheel

motionHint: the screens flicker through their loops, cabs cross the far side of the square, and the wet ground holds and loses each light as they pass
_scripts: Three fifteen-second scripts, one picked per order by the scripted arc (compose/prompt.mjs). Each is three shots at five seconds, written around the objects already in this place, so what happens comes from where it is. Every shot names the person, the first has them turned toward the lens, the last keeps their whole head in frame and ends on them, and none names anybody holding the camera. Tests in compose-prompt.test.js hold every one of those.

scripts.name: The hot-dog cart
shots: Medium. They are at the hot-dog cart under the striped umbrella, taking a hot dog, turned toward the lens, camera holding on them.
Wide. They take a big bite as the screens flicker through their loops and cabs cross the far side of the square, camera easing round to stay in front of them.
Medium close. They hold the hot dog up to the lens and laugh, their whole head in frame, camera settling on them.

scripts.name: The cab
shots: Medium. They are at the kerb with one arm up, hailing a yellow cab, turned toward the lens, camera holding on them.
Wide. A cab pulls in and they open the back door, the wet ground holding every light, camera holding its place.
Medium close. They lean out of the open door toward the lens and wave, their whole head in frame, camera settling on them.

scripts.name: The lights
shots: Medium. They are stepping onto the crosswalk stripes as the lights change, turned toward the lens, camera moving backwards ahead of them.
Wide. They stop in the middle of the square and turn slowly with their arms out, the billboards and screens blazing above, camera holding in front of them.
Medium close. They turn back to the lens, laughing at the size of it, their whole head in frame, camera settling on them.

lookOverride._comment: The most light sources in the menu and every one of them a blown highlight on wet ground, so halation is open furthest here, level with Tokyo. Saturation above the base because the square IS its colour -- red and blue and white panels -- with only a small warm push, since the billboards are cooler than sodium. Grain near the top of the menu: a dark scene shot on a consumer camcorder at night was mostly grain.

ambience._comment: Traffic on all sides at once, heard in the middle of a square: louder and wider-band than a side street, with the quick shallow swell of cabs pulling away from a light in waves, and a short echo off the buildings that wall the square in on three sides.
